{{Short description|Brazilian physicist and philosopher}}
{{autobiography|date=August 2016}}
'''José Acacio de Barros''' (born 1967, Barra Mansa, RJ, Brazil) is a Brazilian-American physicist and philosopher with contributions to the foundations of [[quantum mechanics]], [[quantum cosmology]], and [[quantum cognition]]. 

== Education ==
de Barros received his PhD in Physics from the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Fisicas]] (CBPF) in 1991, under the supervision of [[Francisco Antonio Doria]] and Newton da Costa, with [[Antonio Fernandes da Fonseca Teixeira]] listed as co-advisor.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

== Career ==
Since 2007 he has been in the Liberal Studies faculty of [[San Francisco State University]]. Before going to San Francisco, he was an associate professor of physics at the Federal University at Juiz de Fora, Brazil, and he was a visiting associate professor at the Center for the Study of Language and Information at [[Stanford University]], and has also held visiting positions at the [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Fisicas]].{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

== Notable work ==
de Barros has been a long-term collaborator of Philosopher [[Patrick Suppes]], with whom he published extensively on the foundations of quantum mechanics and joint probabilities. Among his most influential work is his joint research with [[Nelson Pinto-Neto]], in which [[De Broglie–Bohm theory|Bohm's interpretation of quantum mechanics]] was applied to [[quantum cosmology]],<ref>{{cite journal | title = The causal interpretation of dust and radiation fluid non-singular quantum cosmologies | year = 1998 | first = J. Acacio | last = de Barros |author2=Nelson Pinto-Neto |author3=M. A. Sagioro-Leal | journal = [[Physics Letters A]] | volume = 241 | issue = 4–5 | pages = 229–239|arxiv = gr-qc/9710084 |bibcode = 1998PhLA..241..229A |doi = 10.1016/S0375-9601(98)00169-8 }}</ref> paving the way for bouncing models using realistic interpretation of quantum mechanics.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Primordial perturbations in a nonsingular bouncing universe model | year = 2002 | first = Patrick | last = Peter |author2=Nelson Pinto-Neto | journal = [[Physical Review D]] | volume = 66 | issue = 6 | article-number = 063509 | doi=10.1103/physrevd.66.063509|arxiv = hep-th/0203013 |bibcode = 2002PhRvD..66f3509P }}</ref> His recent work attempts to give a neurophysiological foundation to quantum-like effects in psychology.<ref>{{cite book | title = Quantum Models of Cognition and Decision | first = Jerome | last = Busemeyer |author2=Peter Bruza | publisher = [[Cambridge University Press]] | year=2012 | location = New York}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Quantum-like model of behavioral response computation using neural oscillators | year = 2012 | first = Jose Acacio | last = de Barros | journal = [[BioSystems]] | volume = 110 | issue = 3 | pages = 171–182 | doi=10.1016/j.biosystems.2012.10.002| arxiv = 1207.0033 }}</ref> He is also among the main proponents, in collaboration with Gary Oas, of the use of negative probabilities to understand quantum systems.
